blurb.en: Walk along the list swapping neighbours that are the wrong way round; after each pass the largest value still out of place has bubbled to the end.
blurb.zh: 沿着列表走，相邻两项站反了就交换；每走完一趟，还没归位的最大值就「冒」到了末尾。

en: Each pass compares positions 0 and 1, then 1 and 2, and so on to the end of the list, swapping a pair whenever the left one is bigger. The largest value met so far is carried along with every swap, so after the first pass the largest value sits in the last place, after the second pass the second largest sits next to it, and n - 1 passes are enough for n items. [5, 1, 4, 2, 8] comes out as [1, 2, 4, 5, 8].

The swap is a single tuple assignment. Python works out the whole right-hand side first and only then assigns, so both old values are safely held before either position is written - no temporary variable is needed.

Python has two ways to sort, with two different promises. list.sort() rearranges the list it is called on and returns None; sorted() leaves its argument alone and returns a new sorted list. bubble_sort follows the first: it sorts in place, so printing what it returns prints None, and data is sorted afterwards. sorted_copy follows the second: it makes a copy first and sorts only that, so after it runs data still reads [5, 1, 4, 2, 8]. The classic slip is writing data = data.sort(), which throws the list away and keeps the None.

This version is wasteful on purpose: every pass compares all n - 1 pairs, even the ones at the end that are already in their final places, and it keeps going on a list that is already sorted. Time O(n squared). Bubble Sort That Stops Early fixes both. Anything that can be compared can be sorted, so the four fruit names come out in alphabetical order; an empty list and a one-item list come back as they went in.
zh: 每一趟先比位置 0 和 1，再比 1 和 2，一直比到表尾，左边那个更大就把这一对交换。遇到的最大值会随着每次交换一路被带着走，所以第一趟之后最大值落在最后一格，第二趟之后第二大的挨着它，n 个数走 n - 1 趟就够了。[5, 1, 4, 2, 8] 排出来是 [1, 2, 4, 5, 8]。
交换是一句元组赋值。Python 先把等号右边整个算出来，然后才赋值，所以两个旧值在任何一格被写之前都已经安全地拿在手里——不需要临时变量。

Python 排序有两种写法，承诺各不相同。list.sort() 重排它所调用的那张表，返回 None；sorted() 不动实参，返回一张新的有序表。bubble_sort 走前一种：原地排序，所以打印它的返回值打印出来的是 None，而 data 在那之后已经有序。sorted_copy 走后一种：先复制一份、只排这份，所以它跑完之后 data 仍是 [5, 1, 4, 2, 8]。最常见的失误是写 data = data.sort()——表扔掉了，留下的是 None。
这一版是故意写得浪费的：每一趟都比满 n - 1 对，连末尾早已归位的那几对也比；表已经有序了它还照走不误。时间 O(n²)。「提前收工的冒泡排序」把这两处都改掉了。能比较的东西都能排，所以四个水果名按字母顺序排好；空表和只有一项的表原样回来。

lineNotes.en: n - 1 passes. The pass number itself is never used, so the loop variable is called _.
lineNotes.zh: 走 n - 1 趟。趟数本身用不上，所以循环变量叫 _。

lineNotes.en: An in-place sort hands back nothing, so this prints None; the next line shows data itself now sorted.
lineNotes.zh: 原地排序什么也不交回，所以这里打印 None；下一行打印的 data 本身已经排好。

blurb.en: The same bubble sort with two savings: each pass skips the places already settled at the end, and a pass with no swaps ends the sort.
blurb.zh: 同一个冒泡排序，省下两处：每一趟跳过末尾已经归位的格子；某一趟一次都没交换，就结束。

en: After pass i the last i places hold the i largest values in their final order, so pass i only needs to look at n - 1 - i pairs: each pass is one comparison shorter than the one before.

A pass that makes no swap at all proves that every neighbouring pair is in order - and a list whose neighbours are all in order is sorted. swapped records whether this pass swapped anything, and when it did not, the outer loop stops.

On a list that is already sorted, such as [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], the sort makes one pass of n - 1 comparisons and stops: best case O(n). [2, 1, 3, 4, 5] takes two passes - one swap, then a clean pass. A list in reverse order, [5, 4, 3, 2, 1], still needs every pass, so the worst case is still O(n squared). All four demo lists come out in order.

Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 第 i 趟开始时，末尾 i 格已经按最终顺序放着最大的 i 个数，所以第 i 趟只需看 n - 1 - i 对：每一趟都比上一趟少比一次。
一整趟一次交换都没有，就说明每一对相邻的都站对了——相邻的都站对的表就是有序的。swapped 记下这一趟有没有换过，没换过，外层循环就停下。
表已经有序时，比如 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]，只走一趟、比 n - 1 次就停：最好情况 O(n)。[2, 1, 3, 4, 5] 要走两趟——一次交换，再一趟干净的。倒序的 [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] 仍要每一趟都走，所以最坏情况仍是 O(n²)。四个演示用的表都排好了。
和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: Any swap in this pass means the list may still be out of order somewhere.
lineNotes.zh: 这一趟只要换过一次，表就可能还有地方没排好。

blurb.en: Each pass searches the unsorted part for the position of the smallest item, then swaps it into place - just one swap per pass.
blurb.zh: 每一趟在未排好的部分里找最小项的位置，再把它换到位——每趟只交换一次。

en: Pass i looks through positions i to the end for the smallest item and swaps it into position i. After that pass the first i + 1 places hold the smallest values in order and are never touched again. [29, 10, 14, 37, 13] comes out as [10, 13, 14, 29, 37].

The search remembers where the smallest item is, not what it is: the swap at the end of the pass needs a position. Because there is only that one swap per pass, selection sort makes at most n - 1 swaps in all - far fewer than bubble sort - but it still compares about n squared over 2 pairs whatever the input, even a sorted one. Time O(n squared) in every case.

With a strict less-than, the first of several equal smallest values is the one chosen, and the repeated values in [3, -1, 3, 0, -1] come out as [-1, -1, 0, 3, 3]. Selection sort is still not stable: its long-distance swap can carry an item past another with the same value. Stable and Unstable Sorts shows it happening.

Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 第 i 趟从位置 i 找到表尾，找出最小的一项，把它换到位置 i。这一趟之后，前 i + 1 格按顺序放着最小的那几个值，以后再也不碰。[29, 10, 14, 37, 13] 排出来是 [10, 13, 14, 29, 37]。
查找记住的是最小项在哪，而不是它是多少：这一趟末尾的交换要的是位置。每趟只换一次，所以选择排序总共最多换 n - 1 次——比冒泡少得多——但不管输入是什么，哪怕已经有序，它都要比大约 n²/2 对。时间在任何情况下都是 O(n²)。
用严格的小于号，几个相等的最小值里选中的是最前面那个；[3, -1, 3, 0, -1] 里的重复值排成 [-1, -1, 0, 3, 3]。但选择排序仍然不稳定：它的远距离交换可能把一项带过另一个等值的项。「稳定与不稳定的排序」演示了这一幕。
和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: Only the position is updated here; nothing in the list moves until the pass is over.
lineNotes.zh: 这里只更新位置；这一趟结束之前，表里什么都不动。

blurb.en: Keep the left part sorted: hold the next item aside, shift the bigger items one place right, then drop it into the gap they leave.
blurb.zh: 让左边一段始终有序：把下一项先拿在手里，比它大的逐个右移一格，再把它放进空出来的位置。

en: Before step i the items in positions 0 to i - 1 are already sorted. The step takes item i out as key and walks left from position i - 1: each item bigger than key moves one place to the right, and when the walk meets an item that is not bigger - or runs off the front - key goes into the empty slot. [12, 11, 13, 5, 6] comes out as [5, 6, 11, 12, 13].

key has to be saved before anything moves. The very first shift copies item i - 1 into position i, writing over the item being inserted; without the saved copy that value is gone, and the list ends up holding a duplicate of its neighbour instead - the values themselves change, not just their order.

Shifting is cheaper than swapping: each bigger item is written once, and key is written once at the end, where a swap would write key at every step. On a nearly sorted list almost nothing moves - [1, 2, 4, 3] needs a single shift - so the best case is O(n); a list in reverse order, like [4, 3, 2, 1], sends every item all the way to the front, O(n squared). Only strictly bigger items move, so equal items never overtake each other: insertion sort is stable.

Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 第 i 步之前，位置 0 到 i - 1 已经有序。这一步把第 i 项取出来当 key，从位置 i - 1 往左走：比 key 大的每一项右移一格；走到一个不比它大的项——或者走出了表头——key 就放进那个空位。[12, 11, 13, 5, 6] 排出来是 [5, 6, 11, 12, 13]。
key 必须在任何东西挪动之前存好。第一次右移就把第 i - 1 项复制进位置 i，盖掉了正要插入的那一项；没有存下的那一份，这个值就没了，表里会多出一个邻居的重复值——变的是值本身，不只是顺序。
右移比交换省：每个更大的项只写一次，key 在最后写一次，而交换会在每一步都写一次 key。表几乎有序时几乎什么都不动——[1, 2, 4, 3] 只需一次右移——所以最好情况 O(n)；倒序的表，比如 [4, 3, 2, 1]，每一项都要一路移到表头，O(n²)。只有严格更大的项才移动，等值的项永远不会互相超越：插入排序是稳定的。
和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: Start comparing with the last item of the sorted part.
lineNotes.zh: 从有序部分的最后一项开始比。

lineNotes.en: A shift, not a swap: position j keeps its old value for now, and is written over by the next shift or by key.
lineNotes.zh: 是右移不是交换：位置 j 暂时留着旧值，会被下一次右移或者 key 盖掉。

blurb.en: Insertion sort on items a gap apart, with the gap halved each round until it is 1 - by then the list is nearly sorted and the last round is cheap.
blurb.zh: 对相隔 gap 的项做插入排序，gap 每轮减半直到 1——到那时表已经差不多有序，最后一轮很便宜。

en: Insertion sort moves an item one place per shift, so an item far from its final place costs many shifts. Shell sort first runs insertion sort on items that are gap places apart, starting with gap at half the length, so a small value near the end can jump a long way towards the front in one move.

The gap then halves, round after round. The last round, with a gap of 1, is exactly insertion sort: put 1 in place of gap in the inner lines and you get the code of Insertion Sort. By then the list is nearly sorted, which is insertion sort's best case.

For the eight-item demo list the gap goes 4, 2, 1, and [23, 12, 1, 8, 34, 54, 2, 3] comes out as [1, 2, 3, 8, 12, 23, 34, 54]; the nine numbers in reverse order come out as 1 to 9. How fast it is depends on the gap sequence: with plain halving the worst case is still O(n squared), but it usually beats insertion sort by a wide margin. An item jumping gap places can pass an equal one, so shell sort is not stable.

Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 插入排序一次右移只挪一格，离最终位置远的项要花很多次右移。希尔排序先对相隔 gap 格的项做插入排序，gap 从表长的一半起步，于是表尾附近的一个小值一步就能往前跳一大截。
然后 gap 一轮一轮减半。最后一轮 gap 为 1，就是插入排序：把里层几行的 gap 换成 1，得到的就是「插入排序」的代码。到那时表已经差不多有序，正是插入排序的最好情况。
八项的演示表 gap 依次是 4、2、1，[23, 12, 1, 8, 34, 54, 2, 3] 排出来是 [1, 2, 3, 8, 12, 23, 34, 54]；倒序的九个数排成 1 到 9。它有多快取决于 gap 序列：单纯减半时最坏情况仍是 O(n²)，但通常比插入排序快得多。一项一跳 gap 格，可能越过一个等值的项，所以希尔排序不稳定。
和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: The first gap is half the length; a list of 0 or 1 items gets a gap of 0 and nothing happens.
lineNotes.zh: 第一个 gap 是表长的一半；0 项或 1 项的表 gap 为 0，什么都不做。

lineNotes.en: Compare with the item gap places to the left, not the one right next to it.
lineNotes.zh: 和左边相隔 gap 格的那一项比，而不是紧挨着的那一项。

blurb.en: Cut the list in half, sort each half by the same method, then merge the two sorted halves into one.
blurb.zh: 把表对半切开，用同一个办法把两半各自排好，再把两个有序的半张表合并成一张。

en: Why it splits so naturally: a list with one item or none is already sorted - that is the base case, and the function simply returns. A longer list is cut at mid, and each half is a smaller copy of the same problem, so merge_sort sorts each half by calling itself. The recursion mechanism itself is covered on the Recursion page.

merge does the real work. It looks at the front item of each sorted list and takes the smaller one, again and again; when one list runs out, whatever is left of the other is already in order and goes on the end. merge([1, 4, 9], [2, 3, 10, 11]) gives [1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11].
On a tie merge takes from the left list, which holds the items that came first, so equal items keep their order: merge sort is stable.

left and right are slices, so they are new lists, sorted on their own. The merged result is then written back into the list object that was passed in, rather than just giving the local name a new value - that is what keeps merge_sort an in-place sort that returns None, like list.sort().

Halving gives about log n levels, and each level merges n items in total, so the time is O(n log n) for every input; the slices cost O(n) extra memory. [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] comes out as [3, 9, 10, 27, 38, 43, 82]. Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 为什么它这么自然地分成子问题：只有一项或没有项的表本来就有序——这就是基例，函数直接返回。更长的表在 mid 处切开，每一半都是同一个问题的小一号，所以 merge_sort 调用自己把两半各自排好。递归本身的机制见「递归」一页。
真正干活的是 merge。它看两张有序表各自最前面的那一项，取小的那个，一遍又一遍；一张表取空了，另一张剩下的本来就有序，整段接到末尾。merge([1, 4, 9], [2, 3, 10, 11]) 得到 [1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11]。
两项相等时 merge 取左表的，左表里是原本排在前面的那些项，所以等值项保持原来的先后：归并排序是稳定的。
left 和 right 是切片，所以是新表，各自排序。合并的结果随后写回传进来的那个列表对象里，而不是只让局部变量换个指向——正是这一点让 merge_sort 仍是一个返回 None 的原地排序，与 list.sort() 一样。

对半切大约有 log n 层，每一层合并的项加起来是 n 个，所以不论输入如何，时间都是 O(n log n)；切片要额外 O(n) 的内存。[38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] 排出来是 [3, 9, 10, 27, 38, 43, 82]。和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: The base case: nothing to split, nothing to sort.
lineNotes.zh: 基例：没什么可切，也没什么可排。

lineNotes.en: A slice is a new list, so sorting left does not touch items.
lineNotes.zh: 切片是一张新表，所以排 left 不会动到 items。

blurb.en: The same merge, used without recursion: merge neighbouring runs of width 1 into runs of 2, then 4, until one run covers the list.
blurb.zh: 同一个 merge，不用递归：把宽 1 的相邻段两两合并成宽 2，再成宽 4，直到一段盖住整张表。

en: merge here is word for word the one in Merge Sort, Top Down. What changes is the direction. Instead of splitting from the top, start from the bottom: every single item is already a sorted run of width 1. Merge neighbouring runs in pairs to get runs of width 2, then 4, then 8, until one run covers the whole list. A while loop doubles width; there is no recursion at all.

start steps through 0, 2 * width, 4 * width and so on. At each start the left run and the right run are sliced out, merged, and the merged list is written back over the same stretch of items with slice assignment. When the length is not a power of two, the last right run is short or even empty, and merging a run with an empty list just gives the run back.

For seven items the widths are 1, 2 and 4, and the loop stops when width reaches 8. The result is the same [3, 9, 10, 27, 38, 43, 82] as the top-down version, and ['d', 'a', 'c', 'b', 'a'] comes out as ['a', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd']. Still O(n log n), and still stable, because the merge is the same. Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.
zh: 这里的 merge 与「归并排序（自顶向下）」里的那个一字不差。变的是方向：不从顶上切，而从底下起步——每一项本身就是一段宽 1 的有序段。把相邻的段两两合并成宽 2，再成宽 4、宽 8，直到一段盖住整张表。一个 while 让 width 翻倍，完全不用递归。
start 依次取 0、2 * width、4 * width……每个 start 处把左段和右段切出来、合并，再用切片赋值把合并结果写回 items 的同一段。表长不是 2 的幂时，最后那个右段会不满，甚至是空表；一段与空表合并，得到的就是这一段本身。

七项时 width 依次是 1、2、4，width 到 8 时循环停下。结果与自顶向下版相同，是 [3, 9, 10, 27, 38, 43, 82]；['d', 'a', 'c', 'b', 'a'] 排成 ['a', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd']。仍是 O(n log n)，也仍然稳定，因为 merge 是同一个。和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。

lineNotes.en: Runs of one item each: a single item is always sorted.
lineNotes.zh: 每段一项：单独一项永远是有序的。

lineNotes.en: Every round doubles the run width, so about log n rounds are needed.
lineNotes.zh: 每轮段宽翻倍，所以大约需要 log n 轮。

title.zh: 原地快速排序（Lomuto 分区）

blurb.en: Partition the range around its last item so the pivot lands in its final place, then sort the two sides the same way.
blurb.zh: 以区间的最后一项为枢轴分区，让枢轴落到最终位置，再用同样的办法排它两边。

en: partition takes the last item of the range as the pivot and rearranges the range so that every item no bigger than the pivot comes first, then the pivot, then the bigger ones; it returns the pivot's final position. i marks the boundary: everything before i is no bigger than the pivot. Each item j that is no bigger is swapped to position i and the boundary moves on by one.

Why it splits naturally: after partitioning, the pivot is in its final place and no item ever needs to cross it, so the two sides are independent, smaller copies of the same problem. The base case is a range with fewer than two items - low is not less than high - where there is nothing to do. The recursion mechanism itself is covered on the Recursion page.

quicksort sorts in place and returns None; sorted_copy hands it the whole range, 0 to len - 1. For an empty list that range is 0 to -1, so nothing happens. [10, 80, 30, 90, 40, 50, 70] comes out as [10, 30, 40, 50, 70, 80, 90], and the repeated 3s in [3, 3, 1, 3, 2] give [1, 2, 3, 3, 3]. The long-distance swaps make it unstable. Like every in-place sort on this page, the algorithm itself returns None and sorted_copy is the version that leaves its argument alone - the same split as list.sort() and sorted(), explained in Bubble Sort.

On average each partition splits the range roughly in half, giving O(n log n). But on a list that is already sorted the last item is always the largest, so every partition splits off nothing on the right: n levels instead of log n, and O(n squared) work. The sorted demo list [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] still comes out right - just the slowest way. Quicksort with Comprehensions picks the middle item instead.
zh: partition 取区间最后一项当枢轴，把区间重排成：不比枢轴大的全在前面，然后是枢轴，然后是更大的；它返回枢轴的最终位置。i 标着分界：i 之前的都不比枢轴大。每遇到一个不比枢轴大的项 j，就把它换到位置 i，分界往后挪一格。
为什么它自然地分成子问题：分区之后枢轴已在最终位置，再没有哪一项需要越过它，所以两边是互不相干的、同一个问题的小一号。基例是不足两项的区间——low 不小于 high——什么都不用做。递归本身的机制见「递归」一页。

quicksort 原地排序、返回 None；sorted_copy 交给它整个区间 0 到 len - 1。空表的区间是 0 到 -1，什么都不发生。[10, 80, 30, 90, 40, 50, 70] 排出来是 [10, 30, 40, 50, 70, 80, 90]，[3, 3, 1, 3, 2] 里重复的 3 排成 [1, 2, 3, 3, 3]。远距离交换使它不稳定。和本页其他原地排序一样，算法本身返回 None，sorted_copy 才是不动实参的那一版——与 list.sort() 和 sorted() 的分工相同，讲解见「冒泡排序」。
平均来说每次分区大致对半，得到 O(n log n)。但表已经有序时，最后一项总是最大的，每次分区右边都分不出东西：递归 n 层而不是 log n 层，工作量 O(n²)。有序的演示表 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] 照样排对——只是走了最慢的路。「用推导式写的快速排序」改取中间那一项。

lineNotes.en: Lomuto's choice: the last item of the range is the pivot.
lineNotes.zh: Lomuto 的取法：区间最后一项当枢轴。

lineNotes.en: The whole list as one range, from index 0 to the last index.
lineNotes.zh: 整张表当一个区间，从下标 0 到最后一个下标。

title.zh: 用推导式写的快速排序

blurb.en: Split the items into smaller, equal and larger than a pivot with three comprehensions, sort the outer two, and join - easy to read, but it builds new lists at every level.
blurb.zh: 用三个推导式把各项分成比枢轴小、相等、大三段，排好两头，再拼起来——好读，但每一层都要建新表。

en: The same idea as the in-place quicksort, with a different trade-off. Instead of rearranging the list, three comprehensions build three new lists: the items smaller than the pivot, those equal to it, and those larger. The pivot here is the middle item, so a list that is already sorted splits evenly.

Why it splits naturally: the smaller and larger parts are smaller copies of the same problem, and the middle part holds one value only, so it is already in order. The base case is a list of 0 or 1 items; it returns a new list built with list(), so the caller always gets a fresh list and never the argument itself. The recursion mechanism itself is covered on the Recursion page.

Because it returns a new list and never changes its argument, it already keeps the promise of sorted(), so quicksort itself is the function the checks call - there is no sorted_copy. [3, 6, 1, 8, 1, 9, 2, 6] comes out as [1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 6, 8, 9] while data is unchanged, and the letters m, c, x, a, c come out as a, c, c, m, x.

The price is memory and passes: three passes over the list at every level, and new lists at every level. Average time is still O(n log n). A comprehension keeps the items it picks in their original order, so - unlike the in-place Lomuto version - this one is stable.
zh: 思路与原地快速排序相同，取舍不同。它不重排原表，而是用三个推导式建三张新表：比枢轴小的、与枢轴相等的、比枢轴大的。这里的枢轴取中间那一项，所以已经有序的表也能分得均匀。
为什么它自然地分成子问题：小的一段和大的一段都是同一个问题的小一号，中间那段只有一个值，本来就有序。基例是 0 项或 1 项的表；它返回用 list() 建的一张新表，所以调用者拿到的永远是新表，绝不是实参本身。递归本身的机制见「递归」一页。
它返回新表、从不改实参，本来就守着 sorted() 的约定，所以检查直接调用 quicksort 本身——没有 sorted_copy。[3, 6, 1, 8, 1, 9, 2, 6] 排出来是 [1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 6, 8, 9]，data 不变；字母 m、c、x、a、c 排成 a、c、c、m、x。
代价是内存与遍历次数：每一层对表扫三遍，每一层都建新表。平均时间仍是 O(n log n)。推导式挑出来的项保持原来的先后，所以——与原地的 Lomuto 版不同——这一版是稳定的。

lineNotes.en: The middle item as pivot: sorted input no longer makes the worst case.
lineNotes.zh: 取中间一项当枢轴：有序输入不再造成最坏情况。

lineNotes.en: Even the base case hands back a new list, so the result never shares a list with the argument.
lineNotes.zh: 连基例交回的都是新表，结果永远不和实参共用一张表。

blurb.en: For small whole numbers: count how many times each value occurs, then write the values out in order - no item is ever compared with another.
blurb.zh: 适用于小的非负整数：数出每个值出现几次，再按顺序把值写出来——从不拿两项互相比较。

en: Every sort so far decides the order by comparing items. Counting sort compares nothing. For whole numbers from 0 to max_value it keeps one counter per possible value; one pass over items counts each value, and then a walk through the counters from 0 upwards writes each value out as many times as it was counted.

enumerate(counts) hands over each position together with what is stored there, and here the position is the value itself. For the marks [4, 1, 3, 4, 0, 2, 1, 4] with max_value 4 the counters end up as [1, 2, 1, 1, 3], and the result is [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4]. [7, 0, 7, 3] with max_value 10 gives [0, 3, 7, 7], and an empty list gives an empty list.

Time is O(n + k), where k = max_value + 1 is the number of counters - faster than any comparison sort when the range is small, but the table grows with the range, not with the number of items, so sorting three numbers up to a million needs a million counters. Negative numbers and non-integers do not fit this version at all.

counting_sort builds a new result list and never changes items, so - like Quicksort with Comprehensions - it keeps the promise of sorted() and is itself the function the checks call; the demo shows the marks list unchanged afterwards.
zh: 前面的排序都靠比较各项来定顺序，计数排序什么都不比。对 0 到 max_value 的整数，它给每个可能的值配一个计数器；扫一遍 items 把每个值数一数，然后从 0 往上走一遍计数器，每个值数到几次就写出几次。
enumerate(counts) 把每个位置连同那里存的数一起交出来，而这里位置就是值本身。成绩 [4, 1, 3, 4, 0, 2, 1, 4]、max_value 为 4 时，计数器最后是 [1, 2, 1, 1, 3]，结果是 [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4]。[7, 0, 7, 3]、max_value 为 10 得到 [0, 3, 7, 7]；空表得到空表。
时间 O(n + k)，k = max_value + 1 是计数器的个数——值域小时比任何比较排序都快；但表的大小随值域而不是随项数增长，给三个不超过一百万的数排序也要一百万个计数器。负数和非整数这一版根本放不进去。
counting_sort 建一张新的结果表，从不改 items，所以——和「用推导式写的快速排序」一样——它守着 sorted() 的约定，检查直接调用它本身；演示里那张成绩表排完之后仍是原样。

lineNotes.en: The value is used directly as an index into the table of counters.
lineNotes.zh: 值直接拿来当计数器表的下标。

blurb.en: Sort the same (score, name) records by score with insertion sort and with selection sort, and check which one keeps equal scores in their original order.
blurb.zh: 把同一组（成绩, 姓名）记录分别用插入排序和选择排序按成绩排，看哪一种让同分的记录保持原来的先后。

en: A sort is stable if records with equal keys come out in the same order they went in. This program sorts five (score, name) records by score alone - item 0 of each tuple - once with an insertion sort and once with a selection sort, and checks both results with is_stable. For every score, is_stable lists the records with that score in the order the original has them and in the order the result has them; stable means the two lists are identical.

Insertion sort gives [(1, 'Cat'), (2, 'Dan'), (2, 'Eve'), (3, 'Ann'), (3, 'Ben')]: Ann is still before Ben and Dan before Eve, and is_stable says True. The reason is the strict comparison: a record moves left only past strictly higher scores and stops as soon as it meets an equal one, so it can never overtake a record with the same score.

Selection sort's first pass finds Cat's score of 1 at position 2 and swaps it with Ann at position 0 - and that one long jump carries Ann past Ben. The result ends ... (3, 'Ben'), (3, 'Ann'), and is_stable says False. Dan and Eve happen to stay in order: unstable means a sort may reorder equal records, not that it always does.

Across this page: bubble sort (it swaps only strictly bigger neighbours), insertion sort, both merge sorts (a tie is taken from the left) and Quicksort with Comprehensions are stable; selection sort, shell sort and the in-place Lomuto quicksort are not. Python's own sorted() and list.sort() are stable - the program sorted, min and max with key= on the Comprehensions & Built-ins page relies on that. The question here is a different one: which hand-written algorithm is stable, and why.
zh: 排序稳定，是指键相等的记录出来时保持进去时的先后。本程序只按成绩——每个元组下标 0 的那一项——给五条（成绩, 姓名）记录排序，一次用插入排序、一次用选择排序，再用 is_stable 检查两个结果。对每个成绩，is_stable 把这个成绩的记录按原表里的先后列一张、按结果里的先后列一张；稳定就是这两张表一模一样。
插入排序得到 [(1, 'Cat'), (2, 'Dan'), (2, 'Eve'), (3, 'Ann'), (3, 'Ben')]：Ann 仍在 Ben 前面，Dan 仍在 Eve 前面，is_stable 说 True。原因是那个严格的比较：记录只越过成绩严格更高的往左移，一碰到同分的就停，所以永远超不过同分的记录。
选择排序第一趟在位置 2 找到 Cat 的 1 分，把它和位置 0 的 Ann 交换——这一次远距离的跳跃就把 Ann 带到了 Ben 后面。结果的末尾是 ……(3, 'Ben'), (3, 'Ann')，is_stable 说 False。Dan 和 Eve 碰巧保持了先后：不稳定是说可能打乱同分记录，不是说一定打乱。
看本页全部：冒泡排序（只交换严格更大的邻居）、插入排序、两个归并排序（相等时取左边）和「用推导式写的快速排序」是稳定的；选择排序、希尔排序和原地的 Lomuto 快速排序不是。Python 自己的 sorted() 和 list.sort() 是稳定的——「推导式与内置函数」一页的「sorted、min、max 与 key=」那道题就靠这一点。这里问的是另一个问题：哪个手写算法稳定、为什么。

lineNotes.en: Only the scores are compared; the names play no part in the order.
lineNotes.zh: 只比成绩；姓名不参与排序。

lineNotes.en: The swap that breaks stability: the record at i is thrown to wherever the smallest was, past anything in between.
lineNotes.zh: 破坏稳定性的就是这次交换：位置 i 上的记录被扔到最小项原来的位置，越过了中间的一切。
